metadata.title: Seed Domain: Simple Social World
metadata.description: Machine-parseable seed graph for simple social-world relation motifs. This is a first executable social scaffold, not a full model of society.
notes: This graph uses the 56 first-set social situations, not all 134 high-priority rows.
The broader high-priority rows remain available as second-pass extensions.
Adult institutional domains such as law, economics, politics, and history are intentionally excluded.

layers.label: Social Observation Channels
layers.description: Observable social inputs such as face, voice, gesture, touch/proximity, valence, and remembered reliability.

layers.label: Social Relational Invariants
layers.description: Reusable comparison, presence, attention, expectation, response, permission, group, and turn relations.

layers.label: Social Schemas
layers.description: Reusable social event patterns such as greeting, response, turn-taking, permission, transfer, trust, and rule behavior.

layers.label: Social Signals
layers.description: Observable facial, voice, gesture, approval, distress, and permission signals.

layers.label: Agents
layers.description: Human agent handles used by the first social-world scaffold.

layers.label: Social Objects
layers.description: Objects, resources, rules, and tasks that become targets of social relations.

layers.label: Social Event Outcomes
layers.description: Reusable outcomes such as comfort, inclusion, correction, praise, trust change, and rule outcome.

layers.label: Social Abstractions
layers.description: Early abstractions built from social relation patterns.

nodes.label: face expression observation
nodes.summary: Source for smile, frown, gaze, and visible attention cues.

nodes.label: voice tone observation
nodes.summary: Source for gentle, tense, hurried, loud, and reassuring voice patterns.

nodes.label: gesture observation
nodes.summary: Source for pointing, reaching, giving, taking, clapping, and blocking actions.

nodes.label: social touch and proximity observation
nodes.summary: Source for holding, picking up, comforting, removing hand, and physical intervention.

nodes.label: social valence observation
nodes.summary: Source for comfort, discomfort, approval, disapproval, distress, and relief in social settings.

nodes.label: social memory and prediction
nodes.summary: Source for familiarity, reliability, expectation, promise, and trust updates across repeated encounters.

nodes.label: self/other
nodes.summary: Distinguishes own action and state from another agent's action and state.

nodes.label: familiar/unfamiliar
nodes.summary: Compares an agent against previous experience and expected behavior.

nodes.label: presence/absence
nodes.summary: Tracks whether an expected agent is present, absent, leaving, or returning.

nodes.label: attention/absence
nodes.summary: Tracks whether another agent attends, ignores, follows attention, or fails to respond.

nodes.label: before/after
nodes.summary: Orders social actions and consequences in time.

nodes.label: expected/unexpected
nodes.summary: Tracks whether social behavior matches or violates expectation.

nodes.label: response/non-response
nodes.summary: Tracks whether one agent responds to another agent's signal or need.

nodes.label: allowed/blocked
nodes.summary: Tracks whether an action is permitted, blocked, or conditionally allowed.

nodes.label: more/less/equal
nodes.summary: Compares shares, attention, priority, effort, and access.

nodes.label: turn order
nodes.summary: Tracks whose action or speech turn comes before or after another's.

nodes.label: group/member
nodes.summary: Tracks whether an agent is inside or outside a group activity.

nodes.label: harm/relief
nodes.summary: Tracks observed hurt, distress, care response, and relief.

nodes.label: familiar agent presence
nodes.summary: A familiar agent becomes present and activates expected care or attention.

nodes.label: agent absence and return
nodes.summary: An expected agent leaves and later returns, changing expectation and comfort.

nodes.label: social referencing and safety base
nodes.summary: A person looks to a familiar agent when uncertain about another agent or situation.

nodes.label: social affect signal
nodes.summary: Face or voice signals change comfort, uncertainty, approach, or avoidance prediction.

nodes.label: approval feedback
nodes.summary: Another agent's positive signal follows an action and makes repetition more likely.

nodes.label: disapproval or approval loss
nodes.summary: A positive signal stops or a negative signal appears after an action.

nodes.label: distress signal response
nodes.summary: An agent perceives distress and responds with care or comfort.

nodes.label: distress signal non-response
nodes.summary: A distress signal occurs but an expected response is delayed or absent.

nodes.label: comforting another person
nodes.summary: A person observes another person's distress and acts to comfort them.

nodes.label: social turn-taking
nodes.summary: Agents alternate action, sound, or speech rather than acting at the same time.

nodes.label: wait window
nodes.summary: An agent pauses to allow another agent's response.

nodes.label: turn violation
nodes.summary: An agent acts before their turn or speaks over another person.

nodes.label: joint attention reference
nodes.summary: Two agents attend to the same object or event through gaze, pointing, or naming.

nodes.label: object naming event
nodes.summary: A word is socially attached to an attended object.

nodes.label: action naming event
nodes.summary: A word is socially attached to an attended action.

nodes.label: permission request
nodes.summary: An agent requests access or action before acting.

nodes.label: permission granted
nodes.summary: An authority or owner allows an action or access.

nodes.label: permission denied
nodes.summary: An authority or owner blocks an action or access.

nodes.label: unauthorized use
nodes.summary: An agent uses an object without required permission.

nodes.label: gentle intervention
nodes.summary: A caregiver physically redirects an action without treating it as punishment.

nodes.label: safety prevention
nodes.summary: An agent blocks access to prevent harm.

nodes.label: object removal distress
nodes.summary: Removal of an accessed object causes distress or protest.

nodes.label: possession and access
nodes.summary: An agent holds, controls, wants, or is blocked from using an object.

nodes.label: object transfer between agents
nodes.summary: An object moves from one agent's access to another's through giving or returning.

nodes.label: unpermitted taking
nodes.summary: An agent takes an object from another without permission.

nodes.label: refusal to transfer
nodes.summary: An agent keeps an object instead of giving it when expected or requested.

nodes.label: return or restoration
nodes.summary: An object, access, or relation is restored after disruption.

nodes.label: resource allocation
nodes.summary: Resources or turns are distributed across agents.

nodes.label: unequal allocation
nodes.summary: One agent receives more access or resource than another.

nodes.label: fairness precursor
nodes.summary: A comparison of allocation, need, role, and expectation that can later support fairness.

nodes.label: peer imitation
nodes.summary: An agent copies another agent's action.

nodes.label: observed consequence learning
nodes.summary: An agent changes behavior after seeing another agent corrected or praised.

nodes.label: group entry bid
nodes.summary: An agent tries to join an ongoing group activity.

nodes.label: group invitation
nodes.summary: A group grants access to an agent.

nodes.label: group exclusion
nodes.summary: A group denies or ignores access to an agent.

nodes.label: help request and response
nodes.summary: An agent asks for help and another agent responds.

nodes.label: spontaneous help
nodes.summary: An agent notices need and helps without being asked.

nodes.label: help refusal
nodes.summary: An agent refuses a request for help.

nodes.label: promise commitment
nodes.summary: An agent creates an expectation of future action.

nodes.label: promise fulfilled
nodes.summary: An agent performs the promised future action.

nodes.label: promise violated
nodes.summary: An agent does not perform the promised future action.

nodes.label: trust update
nodes.summary: Reliability evidence changes expected future behavior.

nodes.label: rule compliance
nodes.summary: An action matches a rule that applies to it.

nodes.label: rule violation
nodes.summary: An action violates a rule that applies to it.

nodes.label: harm checking
nodes.summary: An agent checks whether another person is hurt after possible harm.

nodes.label: speech turn waiting
nodes.summary: An agent waits for another person's speech turn to finish.

nodes.label: responsive communication
nodes.summary: An agent listens and responds to the content of what was said.

nodes.label: gentle tone
nodes.summary: Soft or reassuring voice pattern.

nodes.label: tense tone
nodes.summary: Hurried, tense, or uncertain voice pattern.

nodes.label: smile
nodes.summary: Visible positive facial signal.

nodes.label: praise signal
nodes.summary: Clap, good, or other positive feedback after an action.

nodes.label: approval withdrawal
nodes.summary: Loss of smile or positive signal after an action.

nodes.label: crying
nodes.summary: Audible or visible distress signal.

nodes.label: pointing
nodes.summary: Gesture that directs another agent's attention.

nodes.label: no signal
nodes.summary: Social signal that blocks an action.

nodes.label: yes or okay signal
nodes.summary: Social signal that allows an action.

nodes.label: child
nodes.summary: Child or learner in the social situation.

nodes.label: caregiver
nodes.summary: Caregiving agent expected to respond to need and distress.

nodes.label: familiar family member
nodes.summary: Familiar person with positive or predictable prior relation.

nodes.label: unfamiliar visitor
nodes.summary: Less familiar person with weaker prior prediction.

nodes.label: peer child
nodes.summary: Another child in play, imitation, conflict, or group entry situations.

nodes.label: adult
nodes.summary: Adult agent who may name, permit, block, correct, or allocate resources.

nodes.label: person
nodes.summary: Generic human agent used for adult social patterns.

nodes.label: group
nodes.summary: Multiple people acting as a social group or play group.

nodes.label: toy
nodes.summary: Concrete object used for access, giving, taking, sharing, or conflict.

nodes.label: dangerous object
nodes.summary: Object whose access may be blocked to prevent harm.

nodes.label: owned object
nodes.summary: Object associated with a person and permission expectations.

nodes.label: shared resource
nodes.summary: Resource that can be divided, allocated, or compared across agents.

nodes.label: rule
nodes.summary: Expected pattern that permits, requires, or blocks actions in context.

nodes.label: promised task
nodes.summary: Future action that an agent commits to doing.

nodes.label: comfort increase
nodes.summary: Comfort rises through familiar agent presence, reassurance, or care.

nodes.label: distress reduction
nodes.summary: Distress decreases after a helpful or comforting response.

nodes.label: trust increase
nodes.summary: Reliability expectation strengthens after fulfilled behavior.

nodes.label: trust decrease
nodes.summary: Reliability expectation weakens after failed or unreliable behavior.

nodes.label: inclusion
nodes.summary: An agent gains access to a group activity.

nodes.label: exclusion
nodes.summary: An agent is denied or ignored by a group activity.

nodes.label: correction
nodes.summary: Another agent signals that an action should change.

nodes.label: praise
nodes.summary: Another agent signals approval after an action.

nodes.label: rule followed
nodes.summary: Action matches a rule.

nodes.label: rule broken
nodes.summary: Action violates a rule.

nodes.label: harm checked
nodes.summary: A person checks whether another person is hurt after possible harm.

nodes.label: permission
nodes.summary: Action access determined by allowance, blocking, role, or ownership relation.

nodes.label: ownership precursor
nodes.summary: Object access expectation built from holding, use, return, and permission.

nodes.label: fairness precursor
nodes.summary: Allocation evaluation built from comparison, expectation, need, role, and rule.

nodes.label: trust
nodes.summary: Expectation that an agent will act reliably in future contexts.

nodes.label: promise
nodes.summary: Future action expectation created by a commitment signal.

nodes.label: rule
nodes.summary: Contextual expectation that certain actions should or should not occur.

nodes.label: help
nodes.summary: An agent uses effort or ability to reduce another agent's difficulty or need.

nodes.label: group belonging
nodes.summary: Access and acceptance within a group activity or social group.

nodes.label: respect precursor
nodes.summary: Waiting, listening, permission, and response patterns that preserve another agent's agency.

nodes.label: empathy precursor
nodes.summary: Other person's distress is treated as a reason for care response.

micro_experiences.title: Caregiver leaves and returns
language_overlay: Caregiver goes away and comes back.

micro_experiences.title: Caregiver tone and smile change social prediction
language_overlay: A gentle voice and a tense voice carry different social signals.

micro_experiences.title: Crying receives response or non-response
events: caregiver responds and picks up child
in another case caregiver does not respond immediately
language_overlay: Crying can receive care, or care can be delayed.

micro_experiences.title: Pointing and naming create shared reference
events: adult looks at the same toy
language_overlay: The adult and child attend to the same object before naming it.

micro_experiences.title: No blocks action and yes allows action
events: adult says no and blocks action
adult later says okay for a safe action
language_overlay: No blocks an action; yes or okay allows an action.

micro_experiences.title: Caregiver removes hand or dangerous object
events: caregiver gently removes the child's hand
child may cry when access is removed
language_overlay: A blocked action may be a safety intervention, not only punishment.

micro_experiences.title: Giving, taking, refusing, and returning toy
events: two children reach for the same toy
adult asks for toy to be returned
language_overlay: The same toy can be given, taken, refused, or returned.

micro_experiences.title: Unequal share and turn waiting
events: adult gives one child a bigger share
adult asks children to wait for turns
a child pushes ahead before their turn
language_overlay: Shares can be compared, and turns can be followed or violated.

micro_experiences.title: Peer imitation and learning from others' feedback
language_overlay: A child can learn by watching what happens to another child.

micro_experiences.title: Joining, invitation, and exclusion
events: group says the child cannot join
language_overlay: A group can include or exclude someone from play.

micro_experiences.title: Help request, help, and refusal
events: another person helps without being asked
language_overlay: Help can be requested, given, given without asking, or refused.

micro_experiences.title: Promise kept, promise broken, and trust update
events: person promises to do something later
person does not do what they promised
language_overlay: Keeping a promise supports trust; breaking a promise weakens trust.

micro_experiences.title: Rule followed and rule broken
events: another person may correct or respond
language_overlay: A rule can be followed or broken.

micro_experiences.title: Harm checking and responsive communication
events: person checks whether they are hurt
person waits for another to finish speaking
person listens and responds to what was said
language_overlay: Social care includes checking harm; conversation includes waiting and responding to what was said.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can a caregiver returning after leaving increase comfort?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The caregiver is a familiar agent whose return repairs the absence relation and reactivates expected care.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is crying followed by no response different from crying followed by being picked up?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Both start with a distress signal, but one creates response and relief while the other creates delayed or absent response.

evaluation_questions.question: What relation changes when an adult says no and blocks an action versus says okay and allows it?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: The permission relation changes from blocked or denied to allowed or granted.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is giving a toy different from grabbing a toy another child holds?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Giving is an object transfer between agents, while grabbing disrupts possession and access without permission.

evaluation_questions.question: Why can one child getting a bigger share raise a fairness question?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Unequal allocation activates comparison of more and less, and fairness depends on expectation, rule, need, or role.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is being invited into a game different from being told not to join?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Invitation grants group access and can cause inclusion; exclusion denies group access.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is helping someone different from refusing a request for help?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Helping responds to need or request, while refusal blocks that expected assistance.

evaluation_questions.question: Why does breaking a promise reduce trust?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: A promise creates a future action expectation; violation causes prediction failure and weakens reliability expectation.

evaluation_questions.question: What relation is active when a person breaks a household rule?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: A rule applies to the action, but the action violates the rule instead of complying with it.

evaluation_questions.question: Why is waiting for someone to finish speaking part of respectful conversation?
evaluation_questions.expected_answer: Speech-turn waiting preserves turn order and supports responsive communication instead of interrupting.
